correctness.finding: PASS. If p divides |A| and n>=2, the base contains P^n for a nontrivial Sylow p-subgroup P, so a Sylow p-subgroup of A wr S_n is noncyclic; Higman's finite-representation-type criterion rules out a serial group algebra. The quotient onto S_n gives the second necessary condition. When p does not divide |A|, kA is split semisimple after scalar extension. Orbiting its central block idempotents under S_n and taking a full corner reduces each component to End(W)⋊k(S_{n1}×...×S_{nt}); the place-permutation action is genuinely inner, so this is a matrix algebra over the Young-subgroup group algebra. Morita invariance reduces seriality to the known symmetric-group classification. In each allowed S_n case every Young subgroup has at most one nonsemisimple symmetric factor, proving sufficiency.

originality.finding: PASS, narrowly scoped. The classification of serial symmetric-group algebras, Higman's cyclic-Sylow obstruction, characteristic invariance, and wreath-product/Morita machinery are all prior inputs and receive no novelty credit. Targeted searches across serial group rings, generalized symmetric groups, hyperoctahedral groups, and wreath-product Morita equivalence did not locate the stated finite-base classification or the resulting characteristic-three family A wr S_5. The main residual risk is that this short synthesis may have appeared implicitly in unindexed modular-representation literature.

scientific_value.finding: PASS. The theorem packages standard structural inputs into a complete and easily checkable classification for every finite base group and all n>=2. The consequence that every finite 3'-group A gives a serial F[A wr S_5] in characteristic three supplies a broad non-3-solvable family beyond the classical p-solvable sufficient theorem. Its value is classificatory rather than methodological.
